title: Embed + Rerank compatibility proxy: unifying pagination semantics, error translation, and backpressure
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a compatibility proxy and adapter layer for embeddings and reranker endpoints to provide predictable pagination semantics, normalized HTTP error codes, and request-level backpressure for legacy clients. This ticket covers the proxy mapping rules, the server-side cursor encoding strategy, 429/503 translations, and a simple throttling mechanism to keep streaming and batch workloads within SLOs.
background: We continue to see divergence between newer unified embeddings/rerank API behaviors (cursor-first pagination, consistent 4xx/5xx semantics) and several legacy client integrations that expect page-based offsets or link-header pagination. Incidents late 2025 revealed ambiguous 429 vs 503 handling during bursts and client retries causing thundering herd on dedicated pools. This work is part of the broader compatibility-layer effort to avoid breaking clients while allowing runtime optimizations (prefix caching, batching) to proceed.
goals: Define and implement a forward-compatible cursor encoding that decouples internal pagination state from visible tokens to clients
Map legacy pagination patterns (page + per_page, Link headers) to cursor semantics in a stable, idempotent way
Normalize server-side errors to a small set consumers can rely on: 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, 429 (retry-after), 500, 503 (degraded-mode)
Provide a lightweight backpressure/throttling policy in the proxy to return 429 with Retry-After for bursty legacy traffic
Ensure streaming clients and function-calling flows are unaffected (no cursor leakage in streamed events)
technical_approach: Proxy receives legacy-style requests and translates to internal unified API calls; responses are transformed back to legacy shape
Cursor encoding: base64 JSON blob with version tag and HMAC digest to prevent tampering; opaque to clients
Pagination mapping rules: if request contains page/per_page -> compute offset window and fetch via internal cursor-aware range APIs; if Link header present, parse links and convert to cursor tokens
Error mapping table: maintain a deterministic mapping file (errors.yaml) used by proxy; include Retry-After logic for 429s and a special X-Compat-Warning header when mapping differs
Backpressure: token-bucket throttler per API key with configurable burst/steady rates; when exceeded return 429 + Retry-After; emit metrics to r-console and a Prometheus bucket
Streaming safety: stream frames must not include cursor state; proxy will strip cursor fields from event payloads and only send opaque next_cursor in final metadata frame
Compatibility tests: end-to-end suite simulating legacy clients, plus regression tests for streaming and function-calling flows
acceptance_criteria: Legacy pagination requests (page/per_page) produce identical result sets and stable next_cursor tokens across repeated requests
Proxy returns 429 with Retry-After under controlled burst conditions; metrics show reduced retry storm on backend by >=60% in synthetic test
Error responses for mapped errors include X-Compat-Warning header when mapping may alter semantics; Sentry/Errreport shows no new noise after rollout
Streaming clients receive uninterrupted frames and no cursor fields in mid-stream; final metadata frame includes next_cursor when applicable
Automated e2e test coverage >=95% for mapping rules; CI gate prevents merging without green compatibility-suite
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy proxy as a split-route for 5% of legacy traffic in us-west-2; monitor errors/latency for 48h
Phase 2: expand to 50% with feature-flag controlled backpressure parameters; solicit partner testing with three enterprise customers
Phase 3: full routing for legacy clients and turn on X-Compat-Warning header by default; monitor dashboards for 7 days
Rollback: proxy supports immediate pass-through mode that forwards requests untouched for quick rollback
risks: Incorrect cursor translations could cause duplicates or missing results for some datasets (mitigate with property-based tests)
Overly aggressive throttling may impact high-value customers (mitigate with allowlists and per-customer rate overrides)
Mapping changes may surface unexpected client parsing logic (mitigate by adding X-Compat-Warning and coordinated partner outreach)
Streaming changes risk breaking real-time consumers (mitigate by isolating stream transformation logic and running canary streams)
Operational overhead: new metrics and alerts required (allocate SRE time)
qa_plan: Unit tests for cursor encode/decode fuzzed with random state
Integration tests converting Link headers <-> cursor tokens across typical pagination sizes (1..500)
Chaos test that injects backend 503s and verifies proxy converts to expected 429/503 per policy
Load test with legacy client simulator to validate throttling and Retry-After behavior
Manual regression: run streaming harness against proxy with function-calling enabled to ensure no event leakage
